# Fix: the colour-click test clicks the wrong position on macOS

## Summary

Two checks in the shell test harness fail on macOS and pass on Windows. The
app is correct. The test computes the click position wrongly for a control
that sits inside a nested panel. This is a test-only fix.

- Branch: `claude/filament-chip`, commit `a74862697e`
- File: `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`
- Build target: `shell_integration_harness`

## Failing checks

Run the harness with no arguments on macOS. Two checks fail:

| Check | Line |
|---|---|
| `a_colour_click_sets_the_slot_colour` | 3302 |
| `the_line_is_led_by_the_colour` | 3313 |

The second fails only because the first did. The colour never changed, so the
chat line carries the old colour.

A third check, `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight`, also fails. It is
unrelated. Do not touch it in this fix.

## Background

The filament menu is a popup window. On macOS the popup receives every mouse
event itself and forwards it to the child under the pointer. The code for that
is `PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/PopupWindow.cpp`.
It finds the child by walking down the window tree and adjusting the position
at each level.

So on macOS the harness posts its click to the popup, at a position measured
from the popup's top-left corner. On Windows it posts to the child directly.

## Cause

`click_row`, at line 2919, computes the macOS position like this:

```cpp
const wxPoint at = row->GetPosition() + wxPoint(row->GetSize().x / 2, row->GetSize().y / 2);
```

`GetPosition()` is measured from the control's own parent. For a menu row the
parent is the popup, so the result is right. A colour cell is different:

- The popup holds a panel, built in `FilamentMenu::build_colour_row`
  (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp:322`).
- The colour cells are children of that panel (`FilamentMenu.cpp:344`).

For a colour cell, `GetPosition()` is measured from the panel, not the popup.
The click lands near the popup's top-left corner and misses the cell.

The call that goes wrong is at line 3298: `click_row(menu, cell);`

## Evidence

I added a temporary probe that computed the position from screen coordinates:

```cpp
child->GetScreenPosition() - popup->GetScreenPosition()
    + wxPoint(child->GetSize().x / 2, child->GetSize().y / 2)
```

With that position, posted to the popup the same way, the slot's colour
changed and the menu stayed open. Two macOS runs, both passed.

## Expected fix

Make `click_row` compute the macOS position relative to the popup for any
descendant, however deeply nested. The screen-coordinate form above does that.

Keep these as they are:

- The Windows and Linux branch of `click_row`.
- The three other callers, at lines 2522, 2942 and 3139. They pass menu rows,
  whose parent is the popup, so the new formula gives them the same position.

## How to verify

1. Before the fix, run the harness on macOS and confirm the two checks fail.
2. After the fix, confirm both pass.
3. Confirm the count of passing checks rises by two and no other check changes.
   My run before the fix: 431 passed, 3 failed.
4. Run on Windows and confirm nothing changes there.

## Build notes for macOS

- A fresh worktree needs the targets `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` as
  well. Without them the harness has no web pages and tests something else.
- Pass the build directory as an absolute path.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:


description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

content.text:
Yes, commit 979302ec6d fixes it on macOS. Before the fix, the two colour-click checks in the shell test harness failed. After it, both pass, and no other check changed.

**The code change.** It is in `click_row` in [shell_harness.cpp:2919](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:2919) and is the change the write-up asked for. On macOS the click position is now measured from the popup through screen coordinates:

```cpp
const wxPoint at = row->GetScreenPosition() - menu->GetScreenPosition()
    + wxPoint(row->GetSize().x / 2, row->GetSize().y / 2);
```

The Windows and Linux branch and the other three callers are untouched. The commit only edits `click_row`, and it added 5 lines, so the checks now sit 5 lines lower than the write-up says (3307 and 3318).

**The test.** I built the harness in this worktree, including the web pages and text catalogs. Then I ran it twice on macOS from the same build: once with the file as it was at a74862697e, and once with the fix.

| | Before (a74862697e) | After (979302ec6d) |
|---|---|---|
| `a_colour_click_sets_the_slot_colour` | FAIL | PASS |
| `the_line_is_led_by_the_colour` | FAIL | PASS |
| `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight` (unrelated) | FAIL | FAIL |
| Total | 428 passed, 3 failed | 430 passed, 1 failed |

A check-by-check comparison of the two runs shows only those two checks changed.

**Open items:**
- **Check count:** Both of my runs had 431 checks. The write-up reported 431 passed and 3 failed, which would be 434 checks. Either that figure was the total rather than the pass count, or it came from a slightly different build. It doesn't affect whether the fix works.
- **Windows is not verified.** I only ran on this Mac. The Windows code path in `click_row` did not change, so I expect no difference there, but I haven't run it.

This worktree now has a build folder, `build/arm64`, and the harness binary in it was built from the fixed code. The logs from both runs are in `build/runs/`.

Yes, the commit fixed it. On a Mac, the two tests that were failing now pass, and no other test result changed.

**What was wrong.** The test harness clicks a colour square in the filament menu. On a Mac, it worked out where to click by measuring from the wrong corner. The colour squares sit inside a smaller box inside the menu. The old code measured from that inner box's corner instead of the menu's corner, so the click landed in the wrong spot and missed.

**What the commit changes.** It works out the click spot using the positions of the square and the menu on the screen. That gives the right spot no matter how deeply the square is nested. Only the Mac code path changed, and only in the test code, not in the app.

**How I checked.** I built the test harness on this Mac and ran it twice: once with the old test code and once with the fix.

| Test | Old code | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| Clicking a colour changes the colour | Failed | Passed |
| The chat message shows the new colour | Failed | Passed |
| Print opens a preview you can cancel (unrelated) | Failed | Failed |
| Total | 428 passed, 3 failed | 430 passed, 1 failed |

I compared the two runs test by test, and only those two tests changed.

**What I didn't check:**
- **Windows:** I didn't test on Windows. The Windows code didn't change, so I expect the same results there.
- **Total test count:** Your notes said 431 passed and 3 failed, which adds up to 434 tests. My runs had 431 tests in total. That may just be a different way of counting, and it doesn't change the result.
